rights.basis: The M5 triage records this entry's code surface as permission-required under the GNU Lesser General Public License v2.1, a weak-copyleft licence, and records its sourceUse as conditional. The plan row elects black-box-respecification with readsSource false. That is the condition this record exists to state: reading the code of this entry was not the route taken to a specification, and nothing of it was read. policies/source-access.json withdraws the M5 gate that would have made reading impermissible for a private author, so the constraint honoured here is the plan's method rather than a prohibition; the licence's distribution terms are untouched and keep their full force, and no source text, decompiled tree or compiled entry of this artifact was opened by this author. Weak copyleft governs derivative works of the code, and a specification written without reading the code produces none. checks/verify-spec-identifiers.sh was run over the specification and returned no finding.

The M5 triage records behaviour as cleared for this artifact, and LGPL v2.1 imposes no behavioural restriction. Behaviour is what this entry's specification states, and it states only what the artifact's non-code documents declare and what the public landing page describes.

Unchanged from the inventory. The licence grants no trademark right, so the project's own name, its mod id, its display name and its content identifiers remain unresolved. The specification therefore names nothing after the original and carries no upstream identifier, and no save-compatible identifier mapping is specified, so a counterpart's alias declaration is empty.

The M5 triage records textures as permission-required for this artifact. Twenty-one interface images are present in the pinned artifact. They were listed and counted from the archive table of contents and none was opened, decoded or viewed. Nothing upstream is tracked or shipped; any counterpart art is drawn fresh from reference under policies/source-access.json and recorded in the package's assets-provenance.json.

sources.use: The claims this record rests on and the second body of evidence the specification is written from. The plan row: artifact CodeChickenLib-1.21.1-4.6.1.526.jar, canonical id RVL-180, owner sdk-platform, rank 23, risk score 4, sourceUse conditional, method black-box-respecification with readsSource false, ten tests. The rights row: licence declared as GNU Lesser General Public License v2.1, family weak-copyleft, assets not reserved separately, acquisition automated-curseforge, publication blocked:unresolved, and the seven per-surface verdicts this record's rights block carries unchanged. The graph: seven in-pack dependents, every edge required and declared BOTH, five at a floor of [4.6.1,5.0.0) and two at [4.6.0,5.0.0), plus two platform edges of its own. The surface census: 806 compiled entries of which 284 nested, 34 tags, 21 textures, one language document, two data namespaces, one asset namespace, 18 entries attributed to networking and 0 to persistence by a class-path heuristic, side layout both by a layout heuristic, no pack configuration or script overlay. The wave manifest admits the entry as a foundation seed with no dependency of its own. One census figure is not confirmed by the artifact: the census records two access transformers and no mixin configuration, and the archive holds one of each. The specification records that discrepancy as unresolved rather than choosing a side.

The disposition governing what this workspace may read. It withdraws M5's reading gate for a private author, so the black-box method used here is the plan's own election rather than a restriction the policy imposes, and this record says so in the code-surface basis rather than claiming a prohibition that no longer exists. Its assets clause is what the texture-surface basis applies: upstream art is reference for a fresh drawing, never shipped, and each shipped asset is recorded in the package's assets-provenance.json.

sources.use: The public description of the project, fetched once over the network and used only for behaviour description. It yields one sentence: a library of systems that make several aspects of modding easier, naming three-dimensional mathematics and transformations, model rendering, packets, configuration, colours and bytecode manipulation. That sentence is repeated almost verbatim in the artifact's own mod descriptor. The page carries no reference manual, no facility list, no integration guide, no side or permission statement and no configuration description; its remaining content is distribution channels. The specification marks every claim taken from it as documented and states in its closing section that nine words of documentation specify nothing.
